items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: And people want to put the Panthers down, like Huey Newton and Bobby Seale and all them.

ctx.x: Guess what? A man with this kind of knowledge. He went around to the machines and was a chip collector. Putting it in — you know, cleaning up. Because they wouldn’t hire him because of his color. You know that kind of craziness. I mean here’s a man, who knows what he could have contributed if he had been given the opportunity. That’s why I try to tell the young African-American kids now — you don’t realize the dues that people paid. And this whole thing about getting out to vote? Hey, I came up through that…

They were just being very outspoken about what they knew that the community needed to do and the kind of racist barriers that were being placed on us. And they were crying out and they wanted to see something — they didn’t pick up guns just to be some kind of warring militia group. They knew that that was the only way. I mean the Ku Klux Klan was walking around with guns. Look I come up in Klan country so I don’t want nobody telling me nothing about the Klan now. These weren’t no Bible toting — they wanted to…
